issues.failure_explanation: The third bullet of Proposition 3.1 is proved by expanding Φ(x^{(j)}+εh)−Φ(x^{(j)}) as ε⟨∇Φ,h⟩+o(ε), i.e. it presupposes Φ is differentiable at z^{(j)}. Since Φ_k = (1/2m^2)|| |F(Qz_k)| − √d_k ||^2, Φ is not differentiable at points where F(Qz_k)_r = 0 with d_{k,r} > 0 (the map x ↦ (|x|−d)^2 has a kink at x=0). Exactly in this case the paper's own derivation of ∇Φ_k breaks and the appendix defers to Proposition 3.1 to define the gradient, which is circular: the proposition cannot both assume and supply the gradient.

issues.failure_explanation: The appendix proof establishes only Φ(z^{(j+1)}) = Φ(z^{(j)}) ⇒ ∇Φ(z^{(j+1)}) = 0. The reverse implication is never argued and is false: e.g. with N=1 and Q nonvanishing, the surrogate minimizer is z^{(1)} = R_1(z^{(0)})/Q, so |F(Qz^{(1)})| = √d and Φ(z^{(1)}) = 0 with ∇Φ(z^{(1)}) = 0, while Φ(z^{(0)}) > 0 for a generic start; thus ∇Φ(z^{(j+1)})=0 does not force Φ(z^{(j+1)})=Φ(z^{(j)}).
issues.overall_effect: The 'iff' in Theorem 3.2 is incorrect; only the forward implication (stalling implies stationarity) is supported.
issues.title: Theorem 3.2 claims an equivalence but only one direction is proved; the converse is false
issues.why_classification: The direction that matters (descent stalls only at stationary points) is proved; dropping the false converse is a local weakening without loss to the paper's guarantees.

issues.failure_explanation: The previous line correctly has (1/2)Σ_k P_k^T∇Φ_k = (1/2)∇Φ in the cross terms, but the next inequality replaces it by ∇Φ, doubling the linear term. With the correct bound Φ(z^{(j+1)})−Φ(z^{(j)}) ≤ L||δ||^2 + Re⟨δ,∇Φ⟩ (L = (1/2)||ΣP_k^T|Q|^2||_∞), the choice δ = −(1/L)∇Φ gives 0, not −(1/L)||∇Φ||^2, so the proof fails. Optimizing δ = −(1/(2L))∇Φ yields decrease (1/(4L))||∇Φ||^2, so the true bound is min||∇Φ||^2 ≤ 2||ΣP_k^T|Q|^2||_∞ Φ(z^{(0)})/(n+1), four times the stated constant.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restore the 1/2 factor, choose z = z^{(j)} − (1/(2L))∇Φ, and correct the constant in the theorem to 2||ΣP_k^T|Q|^2||_∞/(n+1).
issues.overall_effect: Theorem 3.3 as stated (with constant 1/2) is not proved and the constant is incorrect; the O(1/n) sublinear rate itself survives.
issues.title: Convergence-rate proof drops a factor 1/2 in the linear term; stated constant is wrong by a factor of 4
issues.why_classification: A local calculation fix with a trivial re-choice of step; only the numerical constant changes, the rate and method are preserved.

issues.failure_explanation: Q_H = I_h^H Q is a plain average, so a bin of Q with nonzero entries that cancel (possible for a phase-oscillating probe) gives (Q_H)_r = 0 while (I_h^H|Q|^2)_r > 0. Then (W_u^H)_r = 0 is well defined, (u_H)_r = 0, and the coefficient conj(Q_H)/(u_H+|Q_H|^2) is 0/0 at r; the same happens in the coarsest-level line of Algorithm MGPS with coarse arguments. The conventions for 'undefined entries' only cover the case I_h^H|Q|^2 = 0. More generally the coefficient equals (1/Q_H)·I|Q|^2/I(u+|Q|^2), unbounded as Q_H→0, so the regularization u_H vanishes exactly where the coarse probe is weak, contrary to the stated stabilization rationale; only the simplified form 1/I_h^H(u+|Q|^2) of e_{H,k} is finite.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Implement the coarse correction via its equivalent finite form e_{H,k} = −(1/I_h^H(u+|Q|^2)) I_h^H∇Φ̃_k (continuous extension), or add a convention setting the coefficient by that limit where Q_H = 0.
issues.overall_effect: The MGPS update as written is undefined (and numerically ill-conditioned) at coarse entries with vanishing Q_H on nonzero bins; well-definedness of Algorithm MGPS/MGrPIE is not fully established.
issues.title: Coarse-level proximal update is 0/0 where the coarse probe vanishes on a nonzero bin
issues.why_classification: A degenerate-case well-definedness gap with an algebraically equivalent, source-supported finite reformulation; no guarantee is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims the weight choices ensure convergence of MGrPIE. What is proved: Theorem 4.4 shows only that the prolonged coarse correction has nonpositive inner product (≤0, possibly zero) with the gradient of the single-region surrogate Φ̃_k, with no step-size or sufficient-decrease analysis; Theorems 3.2–3.3 assume exact minimization of the full surrogate Φ̃(·;z^{(j)}) over all regions simultaneously. MGrPIE/rPIE instead perform one proximal step per region sequentially on overlapping regions, where updating region k can increase Φ̃_{k'} for overlapping k', so monotone descent of Φ or Φ̃ and the sublinear rate are not implied. No result in the paper establishes convergence of Algorithms rPIE, stochastic surrogate minimization, or MGrPIE.

failure_location.quote: These choices ensure the convergence of \texttt{MGrPIE}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Restate the claim as: the coarse correction is a descent direction for the local surrogate and the exact full surrogate minimization enjoys monotone descent and an O(1/n) rate; remove the assertion that MGrPIE's convergence is ensured.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised convergence guarantee for MGrPIE (and the implied theoretical foundation for rPIE-type stochastic updates) is unsupported; only descent-direction and exact-full-minimization results are available.
issues.title: Convergence of MGrPIE is asserted but only a local descent-direction property of the surrogate is proved
issues.why_classification: The formal results remain valid, but the correction withdraws an advertised algorithmic guarantee; establishing it would require a genuinely new argument for the stochastic sequential scheme.

issues.failure_explanation: From the (correct) preceding line, the right-hand side equals 1/I_h^H(u+|Q|^2), the reciprocal of a bin average. The left-hand side I_h^H(1/(u+|Q|^2)) is the bin average of reciprocals. These agree only when u+|Q|^2 is constant on each bin; in general Jensen gives I_h^H(1/x) ≥ 1/I_h^H(x) with strict inequality otherwise (bin values 1,3,1,3: average of reciprocals 2/3, reciprocal of average 1/2). Hence the proposition's asserted equality of the two maximal update magnitudes is false; only max|e_{H,k}| ≤ max|I_h^H e_k| holds.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality by '≤' (valid via Jensen's inequality applied bin-wise) and weaken the surrounding prose to 'the magnitude of the coarse-grid update is controlled by' rather than matched to the fine-grid update.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 4.5 is false as stated; the automatic regularization selection is justified only by an inequality (coarse update magnitude bounded by the averaged fine one), not by the claimed exact matching.
issues.title: Automatic regularization selection: claimed equality of update magnitudes is false (average of reciprocals ≠ reciprocal of average)
issues.why_classification: The correction is short but necessarily loses content: the exact-matching statement is replaced by a one-sided bound, a limited weakening that still leaves a recognizable (control) result.
